group_guidance.language:
- Prioritise communicative language use, grammar accuracy, vocabulary control, and reading/writing coherence.
- It is appropriate to use reading passages, editing tasks, sentence transformation, and writing prompts.
- Keep the level aligned with the chosen CEFR or learner stage.
group_guidance.math:
- Prioritise accuracy, reasoning, procedural fluency, and problem solving.
- Avoid language-heavy tasks unless they support mathematical thinking.
- Use concise wording, clear numerical prompts, and age-appropriate cognitive demand.
group_guidance.science:
- Prioritise concept understanding, classification, observation, explanation, and evidence-based reasoning.
- Reading or terminology tasks are allowed when they clearly support science learning.
- Keep explanations precise and factually correct.
group_guidance.music:
- Prioritise music theory, symbols, terminology, pattern recognition, and short explanation.
- Keep tasks text-friendly unless notation is essential.
- Avoid overly abstract prompts that depend on audio the app cannot provide.
group_guidance.general:
- Prioritise clarity, broad accessibility, and sound instructional alignment.
- Use exercise types only when they are a natural fit for the topic.
group_guidance.other:
- The subject may be a custom or less common discipline.
- Use only the selected exercise types that genuinely fit the topic and teaching context.
- If one selected exercise type is a weak fit, adapt it sensibly rather than forcing a poor task.

alignment.language:
- The product model for language subjects is Core + Language-focused.
- Use Core sections to check foundational comprehension and response accuracy.
- Use Language-focused sections to assess reading, vocabulary control, grammar/form, editing, or writing.
- Prefer authentic language use over decontextualised drill unless the selected type explicitly targets form.
alignment.math:
- The product model for math subjects is Core + Math-focused.
- Use Core sections only when they genuinely help measure mathematical understanding efficiently.
- Use Math-focused sections to foreground reasoning, procedure, accuracy, modelling, and interpretation.
- Avoid turning the exam into a language-heavy literacy task unless the topic explicitly requires word-problem comprehension.
alignment.science:
- The product model for science subjects is Core + Science-focused.
- Use Core sections for efficient checks of knowledge and short constructed response.
- Use Science-focused sections to foreground evidence, classification, process understanding, data interpretation, and conclusion-making.
- Keep the scientific framing authentic: observations, variables, processes, explanations, and evidence should feel discipline-appropriate.
alignment.music:
- The product model for music subjects is Core + Music-focused.
- Use Core sections for efficient checks of broad understanding.
- Use Music-focused sections to foreground notation, terminology, symbols, rhythm, theory, and stylistic/historical recognition.
- Keep the assessment text-friendly and realistic for a no-audio environment.
alignment.general:
- The product model for general subjects is Core-first.
- Keep the exam broadly usable, efficient to deliver, and aligned to the selected topic.
alignment.other:
- The product model for custom subjects is flexible across all groups.
- Choose only the exercise types that make real instructional sense for the discipline and topic.
- If the selected set spans multiple groups, make the exam feel coherent rather than random.

quality_guardrails:
- Do NOT number the questions or answers inside the JSON. The app adds numbering automatically.
- Do NOT use markdown or bullet symbols inside question text unless the task truly needs them.
- Make the exam coherent around the given topic and learner profile.
- Keep instructions concise, explicit, and student-friendly.
- Use professional, publication-ready capitalization, punctuation, grammar, and layout-friendly wording.
- Matching terms, labels, and short prompts should look polished and academically acceptable on the printed page.
- Avoid repeating the same task pattern with only superficial wording changes.
- Ensure answers are complete, correct, and directly match the questions.
- Answers must be plain text per item, not serialized Python lists or quoted arrays.
- Only include 'source_text' when a passage or source materially improves that section.
- For table_interpretation, use 'table_data' as the primary data source instead of hiding the table inside question text.
- When source_text is needed, choose its form deliberately: passage, article, essay, email, letter, message, or dialogue.
- Preserve clean line breaks inside source_text so titles, headers, dialogue turns, paragraphs, closings, and signatures are not merged together.
- For emails/letters/messages, put headers, greeting, body paragraphs, closing, and signature on separate lines.
- For dialogues, use one speaker turn per line, e.g. "Ana: ...".
- If the source has a title, keep the title separate from the first paragraph.
- Do not force language-only exercises into non-language subjects unless pedagogically justified.
